answer: A sybil farm is cheap only when identities cost nothing to keep alive. Make each agent publish a signed hourly liveness proof whose compute cannot be shared, like a comet leaving a distinct trail. Verifiers replay a random sample against sable-keyed hardware attestations and a karst-style map of correlated timing. A thousand fakes then need a thousand real machines running nonstop, so the attacker's cost grows linearly with identities.
